correctness.rationale: The exact forward characteristic function and compact-support beta-product representation reproduce the same moments. An exact hypergeometric Gauss ODE implies constant, nonzero sign for the second derivative at every interior critical point, so the derivative has at most one zero per half-support. Monotone-factor arguments and central and endpoint asymptotics prove existence and mode signs for all positive rates, including equality cases. The peak-opening prefactor follows from the scaled beta integral for I_e derivative and Euler reflection. SymPy and mpmath code reconstructed both ODE coefficients and tested 410 exact/numerical assertions; finite tests support but do not replace the analytical argument.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Closest published results: analyticity resonances only identify central regularity and beta-polynomial lines; state-resolved reconstruction solves the motor-conditioned law and special binomial curve; inverse fold concerns moments; two-state saturating-speed and complete-graph ternary switching mode theorems use distinct processes. These results do not dominate the asserted all-rate line-graph three-state mode theorem.

originality.rationale: The 2024 source already gives the full stationary density, and related published results already cover the beta mixture, the first analytic-center resonance line and its state-resolved binomial identity. The assessed new statement is the exhaustive all-two-rate global mode-count classification and nonclassical peak-splitting power with explicit coefficient; none of the actually inspected papers and published-record claims imply that theorem. The 2019 equal-rate paper is strictly restricted to T=R; published alternative model mode classifications have different generators. value.rationale: The observable is the stationary spatial concentration-peak count in an experimentally motivated finite-tumble model. The complete two-rate phase portrait distinguishes three center/edge peaks from two off-center interior maxima, excludes unanticipated additional peaks at all positive rates, and provides exact variable-exponent splitting with a closed coefficient. This is a genuine global physical phase classification rather than a routine moment or normalization check; it extends the previously known equal-rate and singularity-only results.
